_meta.what_this_is: What is known for this environment and this need, and how well. Not a judgement of safety, not a prediction for a condition without a test. Team computation from NASA PSI tables and quoted documents.

need.question: Down to what oxygen concentration, and in what range of flow speed, does this material keep burning?
need.reading: A counted test records the material, the oxygen at the start and at least one outcome: an event word, the difference between the initial and the final oxygen reading, a burn time or a burn length. Its pressure is not in the table: it is documented for the investigation as a whole (ICES19.pressure, SAF17.pressure), not read per test. Its gravity level is a constant of the table in the team's source mapping. The count is not a count of tests that burned, and the lowest oxygen tested is not a flammability limit.

top_line.text: Not judged here. This environment sets no oxygen range and no pressure range, so the 133 tests counted for this need were not compared with an atmosphere. Published results and caveats quoted for this need or for fire safety in general: 0 at the oxygen and pressure of this environment and 4 about one of its conditions; they are quotes, not tests. What has not been found in these sources is listed.

sentences.text: How NASA documents treat this question, as quoted items of the reference list: 31 criteria, requirements or definitions and 16 questions or research needs.

Of the 31 criteria, 0 state an oxygen and a pressure inside the ranges of this environment, 0 state at least one of its conditions and none outside, and 31 state no oxygen, pressure or gravity level that can be compared.
The questions and research needs are quoted from documents of their own dates; the list does not say what NASA considers open today.
The six needs are the team's construction, and which items are listed for a need is an AI reading of the items that was not checked by a person.

investigations.title: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II

documented_elsewhere.quote: Pressure was not varied from 1 atmosphere.
All tests were performed at normal pressure (1 atm) and the pressure increase due to combustion was insignificant.

about_a_stated_condition.text: Oxygen margins of safety (low-gravity limit minus 1g limit, % O2 by mole) were negative by as much as -5.75 (lunar gravity, Mylar G at 10.2 psia); the largest at Martian gravity was -3.35 (Nomex HT90-40) and at 0g -4.1 (Mylar G). Normal-gravity screening tests may not be conservative. The low-g limits come from 5 s drop tests and their extinction criteria are not the same as in 1g.
about_a_stated_condition.title: Evaluating Material Flammability in Microgravity and Martian Gravity Compared to the NASA Standard Normal Gravity Test (Olson, Ferkul)
about_a_stated_condition.item_note: The Conclusions sentence of the paper gives 5.75 for Martian gravity; Table I of the same paper gives that value for lunar gravity. The table values are used here.
about_a_stated_condition.tagging_note: '10.2 psia' is written for one of the three margins (lunar gravity, Mylar G) and is kept as words. The oxygen numbers are differences between limits, not an atmosphere.

about_a_stated_condition.text: Limiting oxygen molar concentrations (% O2) from Table I. Mylar G at 10.2 psia: 1g ULOI 21.2 and MOC 20.0; Martian ULOI* 18.0 and MOC* 17.0; Lunar ULOI* 15.6 and MOC* 14.1; 0g ULOI* 17.0 and MOC* 16.0; oxygen margin of safety (delta O2 %) -3.1 Martian, -5.75 Lunar, -4.1 0g. Ultem 1000 at 10.2 psia: 1g ULOI 23.5 and MOC 23.0; Martian ULOI* 22.0 and MOC* 21.1; Lunar ULOI* 21.0 and MOC* 19.9; 0g ULOI* 24.0 and MOC* 23.0; delta O2 % -1.7 Martian, -2.8 Lunar, 0.25 0g. Nomex HT90-40 at 14.7 psia: 1g ULOI 23.5 and MOC 22.1; Martian ULOI* 19.9 and MOC* 19.0; Lunar ULOI* 21.0 and MOC* 19.9; 0g ULOI* 23.0 and MOC* 22.0; delta O2 % -3.35 Martian, -2.35 Lunar, -0.3 0g. Delta O2 % is the mean of the low-gravity ULOI* and MOC* minus the mean of the 1g ULOI and MOC (Eq. 1). The low-gravity limits come from 5.18 s drop tower tests: MOC* is the maximum oxygen concentration at which the flame self-extinguished during the drop, ULOI* the minimum at which it survived the full drop; these criteria are not the same as in 1g.
about_a_stated_condition.quote: Table I: Limiting Oxygen Molar Concentrations and Oxygen Margin of Safety for Different Gravity Levels
about_a_stated_condition.title: Evaluating Material Flammability in Microgravity and Martian Gravity Compared to the NASA Standard Normal Gravity Test (Olson, Ferkul)

not_covered.area: From small-scale experiments to large-scale fires
not_covered.why: Organizing question 5 of 2004 (CP2004.flam.q5); the pipeline does not relate tests of different sample size to each other.

not_covered.area: Detector location and time to detection
not_covered.why: Named as knowledge that detection depends on (TB008.location); no standard variable holds a detector position or a time to detection.

not_covered.area: Flame spread over thermally thick versus thin materials
not_covered.why: Named by the prevention group (CP2003.prev.thickthin); the pipeline carries a sample thickness where the table gives one and does not class a test as thermally thick or thin.

not_covered.area: Flammability limit of liquid fuels as a prevention question
not_covered.why: The limiting oxygen index is named a principal objective of FLEX and tied to spacecraft fire safety (TP216046.loi; see also RG.droplet, FLEX.objective1). The team's scope 'solid' keeps the FLEX tests out of P1; they are counted for S1 only.

not_covered.area: Fire prevention as the stated focus of BRE (PSI-20)
not_covered.why: NASA documents name BRE as the ACME experiment focused on spacecraft fire prevention (ACME14.bre, RG.bre, ACME21.bre). This file links PSI-20 to S1 only, with verdict 'differs', and its table is one row per test day, so no test is counted.

not_covered.area: Ignition delay of the BASS-II PMMA rods
not_covered.why: Defined and reported by the investigators in the BASS-II Summary Report (BASS2TM.igndelay); the PSI-25 experimental table has no column for it, so need P2 has no counted test.
